headline: The Multifamily Operator Stack
premise: Systems of record capture what happened. Grace Hill turns it into what gets fixed. The resolution layer sits above the system of record and across the operating stack, turning recorded performance into resolved performance. Layers one through three follow the renter. Layers zero, four, six and seven follow the operator. Layer five is the only layer that touches both, and the only one that must read from the layers around it and write action back into them. That requirement is why it is a category rather than a feature, and why it is still empty.

resolutionLoop.detail: Pull property, lease, resident, team and market context
Correlate signals to find the cause, not the symptom
Assign the next best action to a specific person
Push the action into the tools that carry it out
Re measure to confirm the outcome actually moved

layers.name: Systems of record · PMS and ERP
layers.does: Owns the ledger. Leases, residents, charges, payments and work orders.
layers.limit: Records what happened. Not built to improve it.

layers.name: Demand and Leasing
layers.does: Attract prospects, run tours, convert applications and price the unit.

layers.name: Resident Living and Service
layers.does: Deliver the daily experience that determines whether a resident renews.

layers.name: Physical and Connected Property
layers.does: Run access, smart devices, utilities and the building systems.

layers.name: People and Workforce
layers.does: Hire, pay, schedule and retain the onsite and corporate team.

layers.name: Resolution · The Resolution Layer for Multifamily
layers.does: Sits above the system of record and across the operating stack, turning recorded performance into resolved performance. Read · Diagnose · Prescribe · Route · Prove.

layers.name: Asset, Finance and Investor
layers.does: Report performance to capital and fund the operating plan.

layers.name: Ancillary and Risk Transfer
layers.does: Move risk off the balance sheet and monetize adjacent services.

categoryMatrix.alternative: Leasing CRM and AI leasing agents

categoryMatrixNote: Signal, benchmark and diagnosis are commoditizing. Prescription and proof are unoccupied, and artificial intelligence does not commoditize them, because they require an owned remediation library and a longitudinal record of outcomes rather than model capability.

categoryFraming.taken: Performance — A major property management system vendor has branded its platform around performance and co publishes performance research with the leading trade association
categoryFraming.crowded: Intelligence — Resident, operational, revenue and market intelligence are all claimed. The word also describes the input, and inputs are no longer scarce
categoryFraming.owned: Resolution — No multifamily vendor uses it. It is the only frame that describes what Grace Hill does and others cannot

categoryArchitecture.promise: Grace Hill gives owners and operators a clear path from issue to resolution to proof
categoryArchitecture.contrast: Everyone can tell you what is wrong. Grace Hill tells you what to do, helps the team do it, and proves it worked
categoryArchitecture.outcomes: Revenue for the manager. NOI and exit valuation for the owner

closingLine: Not another system of record. The layer that makes the rest of the stack perform.

defensibleAssets.asset: Unsolicited prospect experience (Ellis and EPMS mystery shopping)
defensibleAssets.why: Independent, compliance grade evidence no internal system generates

defensibleAssets.asset: Solicited sentiment with depth (Kingsley Index, more than 30 years of benchmarking)
defensibleAssets.why: Longitudinal depth accumulates only with time and scale

defensibleAssets.asset: The remediation library (approximately 600 courses and 800 industry specific policies)
defensibleAssets.why: Maintained against changing regulation across jurisdictions. Not a modeling problem

defensibleAssets.asset: Market context (HelloData, public records across approximately 5 million properties)
defensibleAssets.why: Outside context without the provenance exposure reshaping the pricing category
